newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila shares unable to hold gains by close.
newsitem.headline: Manila shares unable to hold gains by close.

text.p: Manila shares failed to sustain early gains, closing slightly lower on Thursday as investors opted to take profits in stocks which had earlier risen on bargain-hunting, traders said.
"Turnover was not that big and this probably confirms that the gain yesterday was technical," said Leila Calderon, senior investment analyst at Asian Capital Equities Inc.
The main index closed 7.23 points lower at 2,906.33.

Empire East Land Holdings Inc and Megaworld Properties & Holdings Inc posted gains for the second straight day as the market reacted positively to the firms' assurances that they were not facing bankruptcy.
Empire, the most heavily traded issue, finished 1.05 pesos higher at 5.80 pesos while Megaworld soared 18.75 percent, to 5.70 pesos.
In the broader market, there were 83 gainers compared with 46 losers and 65 unchanged issues. Turnover was moderate at 2.36 billion pesos.
Traders said the market may be stuck in a tight band in the next few days awaiting further corporate earnings results and seeking direction from the Dow Jones.
"I think in terms of bad falls, we probably won't see steep ones in the near term," said Teresa Lee, vice-president at Asiamerit Securities.
